routerl 2026/10/12 21:02
It's less rare than you'd hope. Disclosure: I do developer relations at Friendly Captcha, and our widget is one of the scripts that uses generated offline audio (but with no microphone recording) and reads the buffer back on sites that otherwise have no use for audio.

We do this to check whether the browser is what it claims to be, not to track who you are. Similarly, font rendering, floating-point math results, WebGL renderer strings, and whether built-in functions are patched is all much harder to fake. These considerations determine how hard the proof-of-work puzzle should be, and site owners can see it as a risk score. We don't do cookies or browser storage, IPs aren't stored, and nothing gets used to recognize you on another site or on a later visit. The biggest players in automated traffic prevention can't (and usually don't) say this much, because of conflicts of interest between automated bot detection and their other products (e.g. ad sales and IP-profiling).

Your example is really fair though. I chatted with our engineers, prompted by this thread, and we found nothing in our detection that currently uses the audio hashes we collect, so we've started talking about removing the collection.

Also, people not in tech do not generally understand the implication of consent popups.

For example, on multiple instances, my spouse declined "location permissions" an app designed to work with a piece of Bluetooth-connected hardware, and would blame the hardware as being crappy.

"This smart lock app doesn't work."

"You need to enable this permission."

"Why do I need to give the smart lock app location permissions?"

It's not obvious to people that "Bluetooth can be used sneakily by big-enough companies as a makeshift GPS" even if the app needing Bluetooth access doesn't actually need a GPS location.

TheFlyingFish 2026/10/13 06:23
Theme switchers! My favorite example of why "document-only" sites might need JS. Sure, you can use @media prefers-color-scheme for defaults, and you can do checkbox/radio shenanigans to make it switchable, but there's no way to persist that preference on a static site without JS.

If you don't care about your site being static then you can track it server side, but that has big implications for his you can just your site. Sticking a little flag in localStorage really is the best solution, if you can get past ideological purity.
